result.summary: This pull request fixes a race condition where BIP 157 compact filter requests (getcfilters, getcfheaders, getcfcheckpt) arrive before the node's block filter index has processed the newly connected block. Instead of ignoring the request and returning no response, net processing parks the peer's message processing until the filter index catches up with the tip. Once the filter is indexed, the pending request is answered in order, preventing external light clients from disconnecting or banning the node.
result.problem: When a node validates and announces a new block, the block filter index updates asynchronously on the validation interface scheduler thread. If a BIP 157 light client asks for filters or filter headers during this brief window, Bitcoin Core drops the request with no reply, violating BIP 157 and prompting light clients like Neutrino or Kyoto to disconnect or ban the node.

result.card: PR 35354 resolves a race condition where BIP 157 compact filter requests arriving immediately after a block announcement are dropped because the asynchronous filter index has not yet completed indexing. Dropping valid requests violates BIP 157 and causes light clients such as Neutrino to disconnect or ban the node. The PR updates net processing to park the peer and pause further message processing on that connection until the index catches up, answering requests in order without blocking the main message thread. Reviewers (sedited, mzumsande, ajtowns) agreed on moving the logic out of the index and into net processing, and the PR now implements ajtowns's suggested per-peer parking design.
